title: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
summary: Given an integer array sorted in ascending order, transform it into a height-balanced binary search tree.
statement: Given an integer array sorted in ascending order, transform it into a height-balanced binary search tree.
constraints: Return a TreeNode root, not a serialized list. Its inorder traversal must equal nums exactly, and at EVERY node its left/right subtree heights must differ by at most one. Any valid balanced shape is accepted.

target_space_complexity: O(log n) auxiliary recursion, plus O(n) returned nodes
hints: In a search tree, values before the root belong on the left and values after it on the right.
Choose a middle array value as the root and recursively build from the two remaining ranges.
For inclusive bounds, return None if left>right; create the midpoint node and recursively assign its left and right children.
Either middle choice is valid for an even-length range. Do not impose a particular sample shape; preserve all values and balance every subtree.
editorial: A middle element divides the sorted input into ranges whose lengths differ by at most one. Recursively applying that split gives a height-balanced BST and visits each array position once. Bounds avoid repeated list slicing, and the recursion depth is logarithmic. The independent oracle uses a different complete heap-indexed shape and assigns input values to its inorder positions. Property-based grading compares inorder values and checks balance at every node instead of matching either construction's serialized shape.

Root 3 with left child 1 and root 1 with right child 3 are both valid. Both preserve inorder [1,3] and have height difference at most one.
